title: Single-cell, multi-region profiling of the macaque brain across the lifespan
title_zh: 整个寿命期猕猴大脑单细胞、多区域谱分析
abstract: Brain aging is a complex process with profound health and societal consequences. However, the molecular and cellular pathways that govern its progression, and inter- and intra-individual variation, remain poorly defined. We present a transcriptomic atlas of 5.3 million cells from 582 samples spanning 11 brain regions of 55 rhesus macaques (aged 0.5-21 years). We identify age-depleted and vulnerable neuronal populations and subtle, age-associated compositional differences in glia-detectable only at single-cell resolution. We chart convergent and divergent age-associated molecular signatures across regions and cell types, which include sex-specific signatures that could underlie biases in neurological disorders. These signatures overlap those of Alzheimer's disease (AD), which suggests that aging and AD share molecular roots that emerge at different ages and in region- and sex-specific windows of vulnerability. This work provides a temporal, regional, and sex-stratified atlas of the aging primate brain, offering insights into cell-type-specific vulnerabilities and regional heterogeneity with translational human relevance.
abstract_zh: 大脑老化是一个复杂过程，对健康和社会产生深远影响。然而，调控其进程以及个体间和个体内差异的分子和细胞途径仍不清楚。我们呈现了一个转录组图谱，包含55只恒河猴（年龄0.5至21岁）的11个脑区、582个样本中530万个细胞。我们鉴定出易受影响且随年龄减少的神经元群体，以及仅在单细胞分辨率下才能检测到的胶质细胞中与年龄相关的微妙组成差异。我们描绘了脑区和细胞类型之间趋同与分化的与年龄相关的分子特征，其中包括可能解释神经系统疾病性别偏差的性别特异性特征。这些特征与阿尔茨海默病（AD）的特征重叠，表明衰老和AD具有在不同年龄以及脑区和性别特异性脆弱窗口中出现的分子根源。这项工作为老化灵长类大脑提供了时间、脑区和性别分层图谱，为细胞类型特异性脆弱性及区域异质性以及具有临床转化价值的人类相关性提供了洞察。
